Q: VS Code Source Control applies nested repository .gitignore rules to parent repository A:

No, the inner .gitignore does not affect the files outside its directory, even for the same repository. You have to check your logic.

If you want us to locate and isolate your problem, you have to

  1. Design a simplest possible case to reproduce the problem.
  2. Provide the content of both .gitignore files
  3. Provide the names of all the files, their paths relative to the top of the outer repository; for the .git files, provide only the location of the .git directories.

Also, keep in mind that .gitignore affects only the untracked files. If a file was once tracked, it will remain in the repository and will require commit on all changes, even of it is covered by the newer .gitignore file.

You can reproduce your problem using only the local repositories. It make take just few minutes.
